overview.purpose: Help teams create copy for digital touchpoints and user interfaces.
overview.summary: The page defines writing principles for Bosch digital interfaces. It emphasizes copy that is clear, accurate, consistent, easy to understand across cultures and languages, and supportive of user trust in the Bosch brand.

external_basis.name: Google Material Design writing guidelines
external_basis.relationship: The Bosch guidance is partially based on these principles.

external_basis.name: Chicago Manual of Style
external_basis.relationship: Used as the reference for international unit formatting.

principle_schema.name: string
requirements: string

sections.name: Introduction
sections.summary: This section helps create copy in digital touchpoints. The principles apply to all user interfaces and are based partly on Google Material Design writing guidelines.
key_points: Digital copy is part of the user experience.
Interface text should support usability and brand trust.
The rules are intended for use across Bosch digital touchpoints.

sections.name: Wording
sections.summary: User interfaces are direct brand touchpoints. Text should be understandable for anyone, regardless of culture or language. It should be clear, accurate, and consistent.

rules.name: Use simple and precise language
rules.description: Write text in short, understandable segments and keep one thought per sentence.
requirements: Use simple language.
Use direct language.
Prefer short sentence segments.
Express one thought per sentence.

examples.do: Read the instructions that came with your router.
examples.dont: Please consult the documentation that came with your router for further instructions.

rules.name: Avoid filler words
rules.description: Remove words that do not provide additional value.
requirements: Remove unnecessary polite padding when it does not help the task.
Keep UI copy concise and purposeful.

rules.name: Avoid absolutes
rules.description: Avoid words such as 'never' and 'always' when they are unnecessarily absolute.
requirements: Prefer factual, precise statements over absolute promises.
Avoid 'never' and 'always' unless they are technically and legally exact.

examples.do: Your personal data will not be shared.
examples.dont: We will never share your personal data.

rules.name: Start sentences with the goal when describing an action
rules.description: When instructing users, state the goal first, then the action needed to achieve it.
requirements: Lead with the user's intended outcome.
Follow with the concrete action.

examples.do: To remove a photo from this album, drag it to the trash.
examples.dont: Drag a photo to the trash to remove it from this album.

rules.name: Add details only when relevant
rules.description: Include details only when they help users understand the current state or required action.
requirements: Add details only if they support decision making or task completion.
Avoid secondary explanations that are not relevant in the moment.

examples.do: Do you want to remove this image from your collection?
examples.dont: Do you want to remove this image from your collection? You won’t be able to access it unless you import it again.

rules.name: Reveal feature details progressively
rules.description: Reveal more detail about features as users explore them and when they need additional information.
requirements: Do not overload users with all feature details upfront.
Provide more information at the point of need.

rules.name: Address users clearly with second person
rules.description: Use second person language such as 'you' to address users directly in questions, instructions, and descriptions.
requirements: Use second person for questions.
Use second person for instructions.
Use second person when describing something directly to the user.
Do not combine first person and second person in the same label or phrase.

examples.do: Scan the QR code on the router.

rules.name: Use first person only in specific cases
rules.description: Use first person pronouns such as 'I', 'me', or 'my' only when they clarify user ownership of content or actions.
requirements: Use first person for user-owned content or actions when it improves clarity.
First person may appear in labels, option bars, or navigation bars.
Do not combine first person and second person.

examples.do: I agree to follow the terms of service.

rules.name: Refer to UI elements by label
rules.description: When referring to an element within the UI, mention it by its visible label and avoid naming the element type.
requirements: Use the visible label of the UI element.
Do not add the component type such as 'button' if the label is enough.

rules.name: Ensure consistent wording
rules.description: Use the same wording for the same actions and elements throughout the UI.
requirements: Use one verb for one action type across the UI.
Do not switch between synonyms for the same action.
Pay special attention to button labels and UI elements.

rules.name: Use capitalization conservatively
rules.description: Use upper case only for proprietary names, shortcuts, or the first word of a label.
requirements: Use sentence case for labels.
Capitalize proprietary names and official shortcuts as needed.
Avoid title case for ordinary labels.

sections.name: Wording for button labels
sections.summary: Button labels should use consistent, action-oriented wording. Specific labels are recommended for recurring contexts such as processes, settings, and dialogs.

sections.name: Typesetting
sections.summary: Correct spelling and correct character usage are essential for unified Bosch user interfaces. Teams should use the correct character set, spacing, punctuation, quotation marks, dashes, units, and typographic symbols.

rules.name: Use correct spelling and characters
rules.description: Correct spelling and the right use of characters are essential for all Bosch user interfaces.
requirements: Use the correct character set for each language.
Adjust spacing between characters according to language needs.
Use unified and correct spelling across interfaces.

rules.name: Use apostrophes instead of accents
rules.description: Use the typographic apostrophe character where appropriate rather than accent marks.
requirements: Use apostrophe for possessives and contractions where required.
Do not use acute accents as apostrophes.

rules.name: Use double quotation marks for quotes
rules.description: Use correct double quotation marks for a quote and avoid accents.
requirements: Use proper opening and closing double quotation marks.
Do not use accents or single quotation marks for a main quote.

rules.name: Use single quotation marks for quotes within quotes
rules.description: Use single quotation marks for nested quotes inside a main double-quoted quote.
requirements: Main quotes use double quotation marks.
Nested quotes use single quotation marks.

rules.name: Use proper typographic symbols
rules.description: Use the correct typographic characters instead of basic Latin substitutes.
requirements: Use horizontal ellipsis (…) instead of three periods (...).
Use en dash (–), em dash (—), or minus (−) according to meaning.
Use en and em dashes to separate content.
Use hyphens to connect content.

examples.do: To be – or not to be …
examples.dont: To be - or not to be ...

rules.name: Import typographic symbols correctly
rules.description: Use correct HTML or Unicode codes for special characters.
requirements: Use HTML entities or Unicode hexadecimal values where needed.
Refer to the typographic symbol table for correct characters.

units.summary: Units should always be written correctly. For international texts, Bosch follows the Chicago Manual of Style.
units.spacing_rule: Except for degrees and percent, use a space between the value and the unit.
units.capitalization_note: Capitalization matters in units. MWh means megawatt hour, mWh means milliwatt hour, and mwh does not exist. Units should not be written in all caps unless that is the correct unit symbol.
units.warning_example: km/h is correct for kilometer per hour. KM/H is not equivalent and changes the meaning of the units.

recommended_checks: Detect overly long UI sentences and suggest shorter alternatives.
Flag filler words that do not add task-relevant meaning.
Flag absolute language such as 'always' or 'never' unless explicitly justified.
Check if instructions start with the user's goal before the action.
Detect inconsistent verbs for the same action across a product flow.
Enforce sentence case for labels except proprietary names and shortcuts.
Validate button labels against the recommended label table.
Detect incorrect apostrophes, quotation marks, ellipses, dashes, and unit formatting.

high: Incorrect unit capitalization that changes meaning
Inconsistent action verbs in critical flows
Copy that affects privacy or legal meaning
medium: Incorrect button label for common contexts
Incorrect punctuation in visible UI copy
